'''Italo Jose Dejter''' (December 17, 1939) is an [[Argentina|Argentine]]-born [[United States|American]] [[mathematician]], a retired professor of [[mathematics]] and [[computer science]] from the [[University of Puerto Rico]], (August 1984-February 2018) and a researcher in [[algebraic topology]], 
[[differential topology]], [[graph theory]], [[coding theory]] and [[combinatorial design]]s.
He obtained a [[Licentiate degree]] in [[mathematics]] from  [[University of Buenos Aires]] in 1967, arrived at [[Rutgers University]] in 1970 by means of a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] and obtained a [[Ph.D.]] degree in [[mathematics]] in 1975 under the supervision of Professor Ted Petrie,<ref name=gen/> with support of the [[National Science Foundation]]. He was a professor at the
[[Federal University of Santa Catarina]], [[Brazil]], from 1977 to 1984, with grants from the [[National Council for Scientific and Technological Development]], (CNPq).

Dejter has been a visiting scholar at a number of research institutions, including [[University of São Paulo]], [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada]], [[Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul]],
[[University of Cambridge]], [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]], 
[[Simon Fraser University]], [[University of Victoria]], [[New York University]], [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], [[McMaster University]], [[DIMACS]], [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]], [[Technical University of Denmark]], [[Auburn University]], [[Polytechnic University of Catalonia]], [[Technical University of Madrid]], [[Charles University]], [[Ottawa University]] and [[Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)|Simón Bolívar University]]. The sections below describe the relevance of Dejter's work in the research areas  mentioned in the first paragraph above, or in the adjacent box.

==Algebraic and differential topology==
In 1971, Ted Petrie<ref name="Petrie">Petrie T. "Smooth S<sup>1</sup>-actions on homotopy complex projective spaces and related topics", Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 78 (1972) 105–153</ref> conjectured that if X is a [[closed manifold|closed]], [[differentiable manifold|smooth]] 2''n''-dimensional [[homotopy]] [[complex projective space]] that admits a nontrivial [[differentiable function|smooth]] [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] of the [[circle]],
and if a function h, mapping  X onto the 2''n''-dimensional [[complex projective space]], is a [[homotopy]] equivalence, then h preserves the [[Pontrjagin class]]es. In 1975, Dejter<ref>Dejter I. J.
"Smooth S<sup>1</sup>-manifolds in the homotopy type of CP<sup>3</sup> ", Mich. Math. Jour. 23 (1976), 83–95</ref> proved Petrie's Conjecture for n=3,
establishing this way that every closed, smooth, 6-dimensional homotopy
complex projective space must be the complex 3-dimensional projective space CP<sup>3</sup>. Dejter's result is most relevant in view of Petrie's exotic S<sup>1</sup>-actions on CP<sup>3</sup>,<ref>Petrie T. "Exotic S<sup>1</sup>-actions on CP<sup>3</sup> and related topics", Invent. Math. 17 (1972), 317–327.</ref> (apart from the trivial S<sup>1</sup>-actions on CP<sup>3</sup>).

Let G be a [[Compact space|compact]] [[Lie group]], let Y be a smooth [[G-structure|G]]-[[manifold]] and let F a [[G-structure|G]]-[[Fibre bundle|fibre]]
map between G-[[vector bundle]]s of the same dimension over Y which on each
[[G-structure|G]]-[[Fibre bundle|fibre]] is proper and has degree one.  Petrie<ref name="Petrie" /> also asked: What are necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a smooth G-map properly G-homotopic to F and transverse to the zero-section? Dejter<ref name="G-t">Dejter I. J. "G-Transversality to CP^n", Springer-Verlag Lecture Notes in Mathematics, 652 (1976), 222–239</ref> provided both types of conditions, which do not close to a necessary and sufficient condition due to a counterexample.<ref name="G-t" />

The main tool involved in establishing the results above by reducing [[Differential topology|differential-topology]] problems into [[Algebraic topology|algebraic-topology]] solutions is [[Equivariant map|equivariant]] [[algebraic K-theory]], where [[Equivariant map|equivariance]] is understood with respect to the group given by the [[Circle group|circle]], i.e. the unit circle of the [[complex plane]].

==Graph theory==

===Erdős–Pósa theorem and odd cycles===
In 1962, [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Lajos Pósa (mathematician)|Lajos Pósa]] proved that for every positive integer k there exists a positive integer k' such that for every graph G, either (i) G has k vertex-disjoint (long and/or even) cycles or (ii) there exists a subset X of less than k' vertices of G such that G \ X
has no (long and/or even) cycles. This result, known today as the [[Erdős–Pósa theorem]], cannot be extended to odd cycles. In fact, in 1987 Dejter and [[Víctor Neumann-Lara]]<ref>Dejter I. J.; Neumann-Lara V. "Unboundedness for odd cyclic transversality", Coll. Math. Soc. J. Bolyai, 52 (1987), 195–203</ref> showed that given an integer k > 0, there exists a graph G not possessing disjoint odd cycles such that the number of vertices of G whose removal destroys all odd cycles of G is higher than k.

===Ljubljana graph in binary 7-cube===
In 1993,<ref name="bdt">Brouwer A. E.; Dejter I. J.; Thomassen C. "Highly symmetric subgraphs of hypercubes", J. Algebraic Combinat. 2, 22-25, 1993</ref>
[[Andries Brouwer|Brouwer]], Dejter and [[Carsten Thomassen (mathematician)|Thomassen]] described an [[undirected graph|undirected]], [[bipartite graph]] with 112 [[vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] and 168 [[edge (graph theory)|edges]], 
([[Semi-symmetric graph|semi-symmetric]], that is [[Edge-transitive graph|edge-transitive]] but not [[Vertex transitive graph|vertex-transitive]], [[cubic graph]] with [[graph diameter|diameter]] 8, radius 7, [[chromatic number]] 2, [[chromatic index]] 3, girth 10, with exactly 168 cycles of length 10 and 168 cycles of length 12), known since 2002 as the [[Ljubljana graph]]. They<ref name="bdt" />  also established that the '''[[Dejter graph]]''',<ref>Klin M.; Lauri J.; Ziv-Av M. "Links between two semisymmetric graphs on 112
vertices through the lens of association schemes", Jour. Symbolic
Comput., 47–10, 2012, 1175–1191.</ref> obtained by deleting a copy
of the [[Hamming code]] of length 7 from the binary
7-[[hypercube graph|cube]], admits a 3-[[graph factorization|factorization]] into two copies of the [[Ljubljana graph]]. See also.<ref name="quim">Borges J.; Dejter I. J. "On perfect dominating sets in hypercubes and their complements", J. Combin. Math. Combin. Comput. 20 (1996), 161-173</ref><ref>Dejter I. J. "On symmetric subgraphs of the 7-cube: an overview",  Discrete Math. 124 (1994) 55–66</ref><ref>Dejter I. J. "Symmetry of factors of the 7-cube Hamming shell", J. Combin. Des. 5 (1997), 301–309</ref><ref name="DG">Dejter I. J.; Guan P. "Square-blocking edge subsets in hypercubes and vertex
avoidance",  Graph theory, combinatorics, algorithms, and
applications (San Francisco, CA, 1989), 162–174, SIAM, Philadelphia,
PA, 1991</ref><ref name="Jaume">Dejter I. J.; Pujol J. "Perfect domination and
symmetry in hypercubes", Proceedings of the Twenty-Sixth
Southeastern International Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory
and Computing (Boca Raton, FL, 1995). Congr. Numer. 111 (1995),
18–32</ref><ref name="W">Dejter I. J.; Weichsel P. M. "Twisted perfect
dominating subgraphs of hypercubes", Proceedings of the
Twenty-Fourth Southeastern International Conference on
Combinatorics, Graph Theory, and Computing (Boca Raton, FL, 1993).
Congr. Numer. 94 (1993), 67–78</ref> Moreover, relations of this subject with square-blocking subsets and with perfect dominating sets (see  below) in
hypercubes were addressed by Dejter et al. since 1991 in,<ref name="DG" /><ref name="Jaume" /><ref name="W" /> and .<ref name="quim" />

In fact, two questions were answered in,<ref name="bdt" /> namely:

(a) How many colors are needed for a coloring of the ''n''-cube without monochromatic 4-cycles or 6-cycles? [[Andries Brouwer|Brouwer]], Dejter and [[Carsten Thomassen (mathematician)|Thomassen]]<ref name="bdt" /> showed that 4 colors suffice and thereby settle a problem of Erdős.<ref>Erdős P. "Some of my favourite unsolved problems", in: A Tribute to Paul Erdős (A. Baker, B. Bollobás & A. Hajnal, eds.), Cambridge Univ. Press, Cambridge. 1990, 467–478.</ref>
(Independently found by F.R.K.Chung.<ref>Chung F. R. K. "Subgraphs of a hypercube containing no small even cycles", 1. Journal of Graph Theory, 16 (1992) 273–286.</ref> Improving on this, [[Marston Conder]]<ref>[[Marston Conder|Conder M.]] "Hexagon-free subgraphs of hypercubes", Journal of Graph Theory, 17–4 (1993), 477–479.</ref> in 1993 showed that for all n not less than 3 the edges of the ''n''-cube can be 3-colored in such a way that there is no monochromatic 4-cycle or 6-cycle).

(b) Which vertex-transitive induced subgraphs does a hypercube have? The '''[[Dejter graph]]''' mentioned above is 6-regular, vertex-transitive and, as suggested, its edges can be 2-colored so that the two resulting monochromatic subgraphs are isomorphic to the [[Semi-symmetric graph|semi-symmetric]] [[Ljubljana graph]] of girth 10.

In 1972, I. Z. Bouwer<ref>Bouwer I. Z. "On edge but not vertex transitive regular graphs", J. Combin. Theory (B) 12 (1972), 32-40.</ref> attributed a graph with the mentioned properties of the [[Ljubljana graph]] to [[R. M. Foster]].

===Coxeter graph and Klein graph===
In 2012, Dejter<ref name="KC">Dejter I. J. From the Coxeter graph to the Klein
graph, Journal of Graph Theory, 70-1 (2012), 1–9.</ref> showed that the 56-vertex Klein cubic graph F<sub>{56}</sub>B,<ref>Weisstein, Eric W. "Cubic symmetric graph." From MathWorld—A Wolfram Web Resource. http://mathworld.wolfram.com/CubicSymmetricGraph.html</ref> denoted here Γ', can be obtained from the 28-vertex [[coxeter graph|Coxeter cubic graph]] Γ by zipping adequately the squares of the 24 7-cycles of Γ endowed with an
orientation obtained by considering Γ as a <math>{\mathcal C}</math>-ultrahomogeneous<ref>Isaksen D. C.; Jankowski C.; Proctor S. "{{Cite web |url=http://www.cims.nyu.edu/~chrisj/kstarultrahomog.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2016-09-13 |archive-date=2014-03-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140323074711/http://www.cims.nyu.edu/~chrisj/kstarultrahomog.pdf |url-status=bot: unknown }}", Ars Combinatoria, 82 (2007),
83–96.</ref> [[directed graph|digraph]], where <math>{\mathcal C}</math> is the collection formed both by the oriented 7-cycles and the 2-arcs that tightly
fasten those oriented 7-cycles in Γ. In the process, it is seen that
Γ' is a C'-ultrahomogeneous (undirected) graph, where C' is the collection formed by both the 7-cycles and the 1-paths that tightly fasten those
7-cycles in Γ'. This yields an embedding of Γ' into a 3-torus T<sub>3</sub> which forms the Klein map<ref>Schulte E.; Wills J. M. "A Polyhedral Realization of Felix Klein's Map {3, 7}<sub>8</sub> on a Riemann Surface of Genus 3", J.
London Math. Soc., s2-32 (1985), 539–547.</ref> of [[Coxeter notation]] (7,3)<sub>8</sub>. The [[dual graph]] of Γ' in T<sub>3</sub> is the
[[distance-regular graph|distance-regular]] [[Klein quartic]] graph, with corresponding dual map of [[Coxeter notation]] (3,7)<sub>8</sub>. Other aspects of this work are also cited in the following pages:

[[Bitangents of a quartic]].<br />[[Coxeter graph]].<br />[[Heawood graph]].

In 2010, Dejter <ref>Dejter I. J. "On a <math>\vec{ C}</math><sub>4</sub>-ultrahomogeneous oriented graph", Discrete Mathematics, (2010), 1389–1391.</ref> adapted the notion of <math>{\mathcal C}</math>-ultrahomogeneous graph for [[Directed graph|digraphs]], and presented a strongly connected
<math>\vec{C}_4</math>-ultrahomogeneous oriented graph on 168 vertices and 126 pairwise arc-disjoint 4-cycles with regular indegree and outdegree 3 and no circuits of lengths 2 and 3 by altering a definition of the [[Coxeter graph]] via pencils of ordered lines of the [[Fano plane]] in which pencils were replaced by ordered pencils.

The study of [[ultrahomogeneous graph]]s (respectively, digraphs) can be
traced back to Sheehan,<ref>Sheehan J. "Smoothly embeddable subgraphs", J.
London Math. Soc., s2-9 (1974), 212–218.</ref> 
[[Tony Gardiner|Gardiner]],<ref>, Gardiner  A.
"Homogeneous graphs", Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B, 20 (1976),
94–102.</ref> Ronse,<ref>Ronse C. "On homogeneous graphs", J. London
Math. Soc., s2-17 (1978), 375–379.</ref> 
[[Peter Cameron (mathematician)|Cameron]],<ref>Cameron P. J. "6-transitive
graphs", J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 28 (1980), 168–179.</ref> Gol'fand and Klin,<ref>Gol'fand Ja. Ju.; Klin M. H. "On ''k''-homogeneous graphs", Algorithmic studies in combinatorics (Russian), 186 (1978), 76–85.</ref> (respectively, [[Roland Fraïssé|Fraïssé]],<ref>Fraïssé R. "Sur l'extension aux relations de quelques proprietes des ordres", Ann. Sci. Ecole Norm. Sup. 71 (1954),
363–388.</ref> Lachlan and Woodrow,<ref>A. H. Lachlan A. H.; Woodrow R.
"Countable ultrahomogeneous undirected graphs", Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 262 (1980), 51–94.</ref> Cherlin<ref>Cherlin G. L. "The classification of countable homogeneous directed graphs and countable homogeneous ''n''-tournaments", Memoirs Amer. Math. Soc., vol. 131, number 612, Providence RI, January 1988.</ref>). See also page 77 in [[John Adrian Bondy|Bondy]] and [[U. S. R. Murty|Murty]].<ref>Bondy A.; Murty U.S.R.; Graph Theory, Springer-Verlag, 2008.</ref>

===''K''<sub>''d''</sub>-ultrahomogeneous configurations===

Motivated in 2013<ref name="jan09">Dejter I. J. "On a K<sub>4</sub>-UH self-dual 1-configuration (102<sub>4</sub>1, J. Combin. Math. Combi. Comput. 95 (2015), 127-146 (arXiv:1002:0588)
[math.CO].</ref>  by the study of connected Menger graphs <ref>[[H. S. M. Coxeter|Coxeter H. S. M.]] "Self-dual configurations and regular graphs", Bull. Amer. Math. Soc., 56
(1950), 413-455; http://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1950-56-05/S0002-9904-1950-09407-5/S0002-9904-1950-09407-5.pdf.</ref> of self-dual 1-configurations (n<sub>d</sub>)<sub>1</sub> <ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0012-365X(94)90161-9|title=On symmetric spatial configurations|journal=Discrete Mathematics|volume=125|issue=1–3|pages=201–209|year=1994|last1=Gropp|first1=Harald|doi-access=free}}</ref>
<ref>Colbourn C. J.; Dinitz J. H. "The CRC Handbook of Combinatorial Designs", CRC, 1996.</ref> expressible as K<sub>d</sub>-ultrahomogeneous graphs, Dejter wondered for which values of n such graphs exist, as they would yield the most symmetrical, connected, edge-disjoint unions of n copies of K<sub>d</sub> on n vertices in which the roles of vertices and copies of K<sub>d</sub> are
interchangeable. For d=4, known values of n are: n=13,
21<ref>Grünbaum B. "Configurations of Points and Lines", Grad. Texts
in Math. 103, Amer. Math. Soc, Providence R.I., 2009.</ref><ref>
Grünbaum  B.; Rigby J. F. "The real configuration (21<sub>4</sub>)", Jour. London Math. Soc., Sec. Ser. 41(2) (1990), 336–346.</ref><ref>Pisanski T.; [[Brigitte Servatius|Servatius B.]] "Configurations from a Graphical Viewpoint", Birkhäuser, 2013.</ref> and n=42,<ref>Dejter I. J. "On a
{K<sub>4</sub>,K<sub>2,2,2</sub>}-ultrahomogeneous graph", Australasian
Journal of Combinatorics, 44 (2009), 63-76.</ref> This reference, by Dejter in 2009, yields a graph G for which each isomorphism between two of the 42 copies of K<sub>4</sub> or two of the 21 copies of K<sub>2,2,2</sub> in G extends to an automorphism of G. While it would be of interest to determine the spectrum and multiplicities of the involved values of n, Dejter<ref name="jan09" /> contributes the value of n=102 via the [[Biggs-Smith graph|Biggs-Smith]]
[[association scheme]] (presented via sextets<ref>[[Norman L. Biggs|Biggs N. L.]]; Hoare  M. J. "The sextet construction for cubic graphs", Combinatorica, 3 (1983), 153-165.</ref> mod 17), shown to control attachment of 102 (cuboctahedral) copies of the line graph of the 3-cube to the 102 (tetrahedral) copies of K<sub>4</sub>, these sharing each triangle with two copies of the cuboctahedral copies and guaranteeing that the distance 3-graph of the [[Biggs-Smith graph]] is the Menger graph of a self-dual 1-configuration (102<sub>4</sub>)<sub>1</sub>.
This result<ref name="jan09" /> was obtained as an application of a transformation of distance-transitive graphs into C-UH graphs that yielded the above-mentioned paper<ref name="KC" /> and also allowed to confront,<ref>Dejter I. J. "Pappus-Desargues digraph confrontation", Jour. Combin. Math. Combin. Comput", 95 (2014), 101-111 (arXiv:0904:1096) [math.CO]</ref> as digraphs, the [[Pappus configuration|Pappus graph]] to the [[Desargues configuration|Desargues graph]].

These applications as well as the reference <ref name="or">Dejter I. J. "Orienting
and separating distance-transitive graphs", Ars Mathematica
Contemporanea, 5 (2012) 221-236</ref> use the following definition.
Given a family C of digraphs, a digraph G is said to be
C-ultrahomogeneous if every isomorphism between two induced members
of C in G extends to an automorphism of G. In,<ref name="or" /> it
is shown that exactly 7 distance-transitive cubic graphs among the
existing 12 possess a particular ultrahomogeneous property with
respect to oriented cycles realizing the girth that allows the
construction of a related Cayley digraph with similar
ultrahomogeneous properties in which those oriented cycles appear
minimally "pulled apart", or "separated" and whose description is
truly beautiful and insightful.

===Hamiltonicity in graphs===
In 1983, Dejter<ref>I. J. Dejter "Equivalent conditions for Euler problem on Z<sub>4</sub>-Hamilton cycles", Ars Combinatoria, 16B, (1983), 285-295</ref>  found that an equivalent condition for the existence of a Z<sub>4</sub>-Hamilton cycle on the graph of chessknight moves of the usual type (1,2),(resp
(1,4)) on the 2nx2n-board is that n is odd larger than 2, (resp. 4). These results are cited by I. Parberry,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://larc.unt.edu/ian/research/puzzles/knightstour/ |title=Knight's Tours |website=larc.unt.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116230031/https://larc.unt.edu/ian/research/puzzles/knightstour/ |archive-date=2014-01-16}}</ref><ref>I. Parberry "An efficient algorithm for the Knight's tour problem", Discrete Applied Mathematics, 73, (1997), 251-260
</ref> in relation to the algorithmic aspects of the knight's tour problem.

In 1985, Dejter<ref>Dejter I. J. "Hamilton cycles and quotients of bipartite graphs", in Y. Alavi et al., eds., Graph Theory and its Appl. to Alg. and Comp. Sci., Wyley, 1985, 189-199.</ref> presented a construction technique for Hamilton cycles in the [[Gray code|middle-levels graphs]]. The existence of such cycles had been conjectured by I. Havel in 1983.<ref>Havel I. "Semipaths in directed cubes", in: M. Fiedler (Ed.), Graphs and other Combinatorial Topics, Teubner-Texte Math., Teubner, Leipzig, 1983, pp. 101–108.</ref> and by M. Buck and D. Wiedemann in 1984,<ref>Buck M. and Wiedemann D. "Gray codes with restricted density", Discrete Math., 48 (1984), 163-–171.</ref> (though [[Béla Bollobás]] presented it to Dejter as a [[Paul Erdős]]' conjecture in Jan. 1983) and established by T. Mütze<ref>Mütze T. "Proof of the middle-levels conjecture", Proc. Lond. Math. Soc (3) 112 (2016), 677-713 (Arxiv 1404:4442</ref> in 2014. That technique was used by Dejter et al.<ref>Dejter I. J. "Stratification for hamiltonicity", Congressus Numeranium, 47 (1985) 265-272.</ref><ref>Dejter I. J.; Quintana J. "Long cycles in revolving door graphs", Congressus Numerantium, 60 (1987), 163-168.</ref><ref>Dejter I. J.;  Cordova J; Quintana J. "Two Hamilton cycles in bipartite reflective Kneser graphs", Discrete Math. 72 (1988) 63-70.</ref><ref>Dejter I. J.; Quintana J. "On an extension of a conjecture of I. Havel", in Y. Alavi et al. eds., Graph Theory, Combin. and Appl., J. Wiley 1991, vol I, 327-342.</ref><ref>Dejter I. J.; Cedeno W.; Jauregui V. "Frucht diagrams, Boolean graphs and Hamilton cycles", Scientia, Ser. A, Math. Sci., 5 (1992/93) 21-37.</ref><ref>Dejter I. J.; Cedeno W.; Jauregui V. "A note on F-diagrams, Boolean graphs and Hamilton cycles", Discrete Math. 114 (1993), 131-135.</ref>

In 2014, Dejter<ref>Dejter I. J. "Ordering the Levels L<sub>k</sub> and L<sub>k+1</sub> of B<sub>2k+1</sub>".</ref> returned to this problem and established a canonical ordering of the vertices in a quotient graph (of each middle-levels graph under the action of a [[dihedral group]]) in one-to-one correspondence with an initial section of a system of numeration (present as sequence A239903 in the [[On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences]] by [[Neil Sloane]])
<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A239903}}</ref> composed by restricted growth strings<ref>Ruskey F. "Simple combinatorial Gray codes constructed by reversing sublists", Lecture Notes in Computer Science, 762 (1993) 201-208.</ref><ref name="G-s">Arndt J., Matters Computational: Ideas, Algorithms, Source Code, Springer, 2011.</ref> (with the k-th [[Catalan number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000108}}</ref> expressed by means of the string 10...0 with k "zeros" and a single "one", as J. Arndt does in page 325 <ref name="G-s" />) and related to Kierstead-Trotter lexical matching colors.<ref>Kierstead  H. A.; [[William T. Trotter|Trotter W. T.]] "Explicit matchings in the middle two levels of the boolean lattice", Order 5 (1988), 163-171.</ref> This system of numeration may apply to a dihedral-symmetric restricted version of the middle-levels conjecture.

In 1988, Dejter<ref>I. J. Dejter "Minimal hamiltonian and nonhamiltonian covering graphs of K<sub>n</sub>", Ars Combinatoria, 25-C, (1988), 63-71.</ref> showed that for any positive integer n, all 2-covering graphs of the [[complete graph]] K<sub>n</sub> on n vertices
can be determined; in addition, he showed that among them there is only one graph that is connected and has a maximal automorphism group, which happens to be bipartite; Dejter also showed that an i-covering graph of K<sub>n</sub> is hamiltonian, for i less than 4, and that properly minimal connected non-hamiltonian covering graphs of K<sub>n</sub> are obtained which are 4-coverings
of K<sub>n</sub>; also, non-hamiltonian connected 6-coverings of K<sub>n</sub>
were constructed in that work.

Also in 1988, Dejter<ref>I. J. Dejter "(1,2k)-Chessknight Hamilton cycles invariant under quarter turns", Scientia, Ser. A, Math. Sci., 2 (1988), 39-51.</ref> showed that if k, n and q are integers such that if 0 &lt;2k&lt;n=2kq<math>\pm</math>1, then the graph generated by the generalized chessknight moves of type (1,2k) on the 2n x 2n-chessboard has Hamilton cycles invariant under quarter turns. For k=1,  respectively 2, this extends to the following necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of such cycles: that  n is odd and larger than 2k-1.

In 1990, Dejter<ref>I. J. Dejter "Quarter-turns and Hamilton cycles for annular chessknight graphs", Scientia, Ser. A, Math. Sci., 4 (1990/91), 21-29.</ref> showed that if n and r are integers larger than 0 with n+r larger than 2, then the difference of two concentric square boards A and B with (n + 2r)<sup>2</sup> and n<sup>2</sup> entries respectively has a chessknight Hamilton cycle invariant under quarter-turns [[if and only if]] r is larger than 2 and either n or r is odd.

In 1991, Dejter and [[Victor Neumann-Lara|Neumann-Lara]]<ref>I. J. Dejter and V. Neumann-Lara "Voltage graphs and Hamilton cycles", in V.  Kulli ed., Advances in Graph Theory, Vishwa Int. Publ., Gulbarga, India, 1991, 141-153.</ref> showed that given a group Z<sub>n</sub> acting freely on a graph G, the notion of a voltage graph<ref>J.L. Gross and T.W. Tucker "Topological Graph Theory" Wiley, New York (1987).</ref> is applied to the search for Hamilton cycles in G invariant under an action of Z<sub>n</sub> on G. As an application, for n = 2 and 4, equivalent conditions and lower bounds for chessknight Hamilton cycles containing paths spanning square quadrants and rectangular half-boards were found, respectively.

=== Coloring the arcs of biregular graphs ===
Recalling that each edge of a graph H has two oppositely oriented arcs, each vertex v of H is identified with the set of arcs (v,e) departing from v along the edges e of H incident to v. Let H be a (λ,&mu;)-[[biregular graph]] with [[Bipartite graph|bipartition]] (Y,X), where |Y|=k&mu; and |X|=kλ, where k&lt;0, λ and &mu; are integers. In,<ref>I. J. Dejter "On Coloring the Arcs of Biregular Graphs", Discrete Applied Mathematics 284 (2020) 489--498</ref> Dejter considered the problem of assigning, for each edge e=yx of H, a color given by an element of Y, respectively X, to the arc (y,e), respectively (x,e), so that each color is assigned exactly once in the set of arcs departing from each vertex of H. Furthermore, Dejter set such assignment to fulfill a specific bicolor [[weight function]] over a [[Monotonic function|monotonic subset]] of Y×X, pointing that this problem applies to the [[Design of Experiments]] for [[Industrial Chemistry]], [[Molecular Biology]], [[Cellular neuroscience|Cellular Neuroscience]], etc. An algorithmic construction based on [[biregular graph]]s with bipartitions given by [[Cyclic group|cyclic-group]] pairs is also presented in Dejter's work, as well as three essentially different solutions to the Great Circle Challenge Puzzle based on a different [[biregular graph]] whose bipartition is formed by the vertices and 5-cycles of the [[Petersen graph]].

==Perfect dominating sets==
A perfect [[dominating set]] S of a graph G is a set of vertices of G such that every vertex of G is either in S or is adjacent to exactly one vertex of S. Weichsel<ref name="WW">Weichsel P. "Dominating sets in n-cubes", Jour. of Graph Theory, 18 (1994), 479-488</ref> showed that a perfect dominating set of the n-[[hypercubes|cube]] Q<sub>n</sub> induces a subgraph of Q<sub>n</sub> whose components are isomorphic to [[hypercubes]] and conjectured that each of these [[hypercubes]] has the same dimension. In 1993, Dejter and Weichsel<ref name="W" /> presented the first known cases in which those components have the same dimension but different directions, namely in the 8-cube with components that are 1-cubes formed each by one edge, with the involved edges happening in:

(a) four different directions, as told by Alexander Felzenbaum to Weichsel in Rehovot, Israel, 1988;

(b) eight different directions, which involves the [[Hamming code]] of length 7, the [[Heawood graph]], the [[Fano plane]] and the [[Steiner triple system]] of order 7.

The result of (a) above is immediately extended to perfect dominating sets in cubes of dimensions which are powers of 2 whose components contain each an only edge in half the coordinate direction. On the other hand, in 1991, Dejter and Phelps<ref>Dejter. I. J.; Phelps K. T. "On perfect domination of binary cubes", 
preprint.</ref> extended the result of (b) above again to cubes whose dimensions are powers of 2, with components composed each by a unique edge in all coordinate directions. (However, this result is not yet extended to q-ary cubes, as planned by the authors).

The Weichsel conjecture<ref name="WW" /> was answered in the affirmative by Östergård and Weakley,<ref>Östergård P.; Weakley W. D. "Constructing covering codes with given automorphisms", Des. Codes Cryptogr. 16 (1999), 65-73</ref> who found a perfect dominating set in the 13-cube whose components are 26 4-cubes and 288 isolated vertices. Dejter and Phelps<ref>Dejter I. J.; Phelps K. T. "Ternary Hamming and Binary Perfect Covering Codes", in: A. Barg and S.
Litsyn, eds., Codes and Association Schemes, DIMACS Ser. Discrete Math. Theoret. Comput Sci. 56, Amer. Math. Soc., Providence, RI, 111--113"</ref> gave a short and elegant proof of this result.

===Efficient dominating sets===
An E-chain is a countable family of nested graphs, each of which has
an efficient dominating set. The Hamming codes in the n-cubes
provide a classical example of E-chains. Dejter and Serra<ref
name="DS">Dejter I. J.; Serra O. "Efficient dominating sets in Cayley graphs", Discrete Appl. Math., 129 (2003), no. 2-3, 319-328.</ref> gave a constructing tool to produce E-chains of Cayley graphs. This tool was used to construct infinite families of E-chains of Cayley graphs generated by transposition trees of diameter 2 on symmetric groups. These graphs, known as star graphs,<ref name="AK">Akers S.B.; Krishnamurthy  B. "A group theoretic model for symmetric interconnection networks", IEEE Trans. Comput., 38 (1989), 555-565.</ref> had the efficient domination property established by Arumugam and Kala.<ref>Arumugam S.; Kala R. "Domination Parameters of Star Graphs", Ars Combinatoria, 44 (1996) 93-96</ref>
In contrast, Dejter and O. Tomaiconza<ref name="DO">Dejter I. J.; Tomaiconza O. "Nonexistence of Efficient Dominating Sets in the Cayley Graphs Generated by Transposition Trees of Diameter 3", Discrete Appl. Math., 232 (2017), 116-124.</ref> showed that there is no efficient dominating set in any Cayley graph generated by a transposition tree of diameter 3. Further study on threaded distance trees and E-sets of star graphs was conducted by Dejter.<ref>Dejter I. J. "Star
graphs: threaded distance trees and E-sets", J. Combin. Math.
Combin. Comput. 77 (2011), 3-16.</ref> In 2012, Dejter adapted the results cited above to the case of [[Directed graph|digraphs]].<ref>Dejter I. J.
"Worst-case efficient dominating sets in digraphs", Discrete Applied
Mathematics, 161 (2013) 944–952. First Online DOI 10.1016/j.dam.2012.11.016</ref> In fact, worst-case efficient dominating sets in digraphs are conceived
so that their presence in certain strong digraphs corresponds to
that of efficient dominating sets in star graphs. The fact that the
star graphs form a so-called dense segmental neighborly E-chain<ref
name="DS" /> is reflected in a corresponding fact for digraphs.

===Quasiperfect dominating sets===

In 2009,<ref>Dejter I. J. "Quasiperfect domination in triangular lattices",
Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory, 29(1) (2009),
179-198.</ref> Dejter defined a vertex subset S of a graph G as a
quasiperfect dominating set in G if each vertex v of G not in S
is adjacent to d<sub>v</sub>&nbsp;&isin;{1,2} vertices of S, and then
investigated perfect and quasiperfect dominating sets in the regular
tessellation graph of [[Schläfli symbol]] {3,6} and in its toroidal
quotient graphs, yielding the classification of their perfect dominating
sets and most of their quasiperfect dominating sets S with induced
components of the form K<sub>&nu;</sub>, where
&nu;&nbsp;&isin;{1,2,3} depends only on S.

==Coding theory==

===Invariants of perfect error-correcting codes===
Invariants of perfect error-correcting codes were addressed by
Dejter in,<ref>Dejter I. J. "SQS-graphs of extended 1-perfect
codes", Congressus Numerantium, 193 (2008), 175-194.</ref><ref>Dejter I. J. "STS-Graphical invariant for perfect codes", J.
Combin. Math. Combin. Comput., 36 (2001), 65-82.</ref> and Dejter and Delgado<ref>Dejter I. J.; Delgado A. A. "STS-Graphs of perfect codes mod
kernel", Discrete Mathematics, 253 (2005), 31-47.</ref> in which it
is shown that a perfect 1-error-correcting code C is 'foldable' over
its kernel via the Steiner triple systems associated to its
codewords. The resulting 'folding' produces a graph invariant for C
via Pasch configurations and tensors. Moreover, the invariant is
complete for Vasil'ev codes<ref>Vasil'ev Y. L. "On nongroup
close-packed codes", Problem of Cybernetics, 8 (1962) 375-378 (in
Russian).</ref> of length 15 as viewed by F. Hergert,<ref>Hergert F,
"The equivalence classes of the Vasil'ev codes of length 15",
Springer-Verlag Lecture Notes 969 (1982) 176-186.</ref> showing the
existence of nonadditive propelinear 1-perfect codes,<ref>Rifà J.;
Basart J. M.; Huguet L. "On completely regular propelinear codes"
AAECC (1988) 341-355</ref><ref>Rifà J.; Pujol J. "Translation
invariant propelinear codes, Transact. Info. Th., IEEE, 43(1997)
590-598.</ref> and allowing to visualize a propelinear code by means
of the commutative group formed by its classes mod kernel, as well
as to generalize the notion of a propelinear code by extending the
involved composition of permutations to a more general group
product.

===Generalizing perfect Lee codes===
Motivated by an application problem in computer architecture,
Araujo, Dejter and Horak<ref name="ADH">Araujo C; Dejter I. J.; Horak P.
"generalization of Lee codes", Designs, Codes and Cryptography,
70 77-90 (2014).</ref> introduced
a notion of perfect distance-dominating set, PDDS, in a graph,
constituting a generalization of perfect Lee codes,<ref name="GW">Golomb
S. W.; Welsh L. R. "Perfect codes in the Lee metric and the packing
of polyominoes", SIAM J. Applied Math. 18 (1970), 302-317.</ref>
diameter perfect codes,<ref name="HA">Horak, P.; AlBdaiwi, B.F
"Diameter Perfect Lee Codes", IEEE Transactions on Information
Theory 58-8 (2012), 5490-5499.</ref> and other codes and dominating
sets, and thus initiating a systematic study of such vertex sets.
Some of these sets, related to the motivating application, were constructed, and the
non-existence of others was demonstrated. In fact, an extension of the
long-standing Golomb-Welch Conjecture,<ref name="GW" /> in terms of
PDDSs, was stated.

===Total perfect codes===
According to Dejter and Delgado,<ref name="DD">Dejter I. J.; Delgado A. A.
"Perfect domination in rectangular grid graphs", J. Combin. Math.
Combin. Comput., 70 (2009), 177-196.</ref> given a vertex subset S'
of a side P<sub>m</sub> of an m x n grid graph G, the perfect dominating sets
S in G with S' being the intersection of S with V(P<sub>m</sub>) can be
determined via an exhaustive algorithm of running time O(2<sup>m+n</sup>).
Extending the algorithm to infinite-grid graphs of width m-1,
periodicity makes the binary decision tree prunable into a finite
threaded tree, a closed walk of which yields all such sets S. The
graphs induced by the complements of such sets S can be codified by
arrays of ordered pairs of positive integers, for the growth and
determination of which a speedier algorithm exists. A recent
characterization of grid graphs having '''total perfect codes''' S (i.e. with just 1-cubes as induced components, also called 
1-PDDS<ref name="ADH" /> and DPL(2,4)<ref name="HA" />), due to Klostermeyer and
Goldwasser,<ref>Klostermeyer W. F.; Goldwasser J. L. "Total Perfect
Codes in Grid Graphs", Bull. Inst. Comb. Appl., 46(2006)
61-68.</ref> allowed Dejter and Delgado<ref name="DD" /> to show that
these sets S are restrictions of only one total perfect code S<sub>1</sub> in
the planar integer lattice graph, with the extra-bonus that the
complement of S<sub>1</sub> yields an aperiodic tiling, like the Penrose
tiling. In contrast, the parallel, horizontal, total perfect codes
in the planar integer lattice graph are in 1-1 correspondence with
the doubly infinite {0,1}-sequences.

Dejter showed<ref>Dejter I. J. "Perfect domination in regular grid
graphs", Austral. Jour. Combin., 42 (2008), 99-114</ref> that there
is an uncountable number of parallel total perfect codes in the
planar integer lattice graph L; in contrast, there is just
one 1-perfect code, and just one total perfect code in L, the latter code
restricting to total perfect codes of rectangular grid graphs
(which yields an asymmetric, Penrose, tiling of the plane); in
particular, Dejter characterized all cycle products C<sub>m</sub> x C<sub>n</sub>
containing parallel total perfect codes, and the d-perfect and total
perfect code partitions of L and C<sub>m</sub> x C<sub>n</sub>, the former having as
quotient graph the undirected Cayley graphs of the cyclic group of
order 2d<sup>2</sup>+2d+1 with generator set {1,2d<sup>2</sup>}.

In 2012, Araujo and Dejter<ref>Dejter I. J.; Araujo C. "Lattice-like
total perfect codes", Discussiones Mathematicae Graph Theory,
34 (2014) 57–74,
doi:10.7151/dmgt.1715.</ref> made a conjecturing
contribution to the classification of lattice-like total perfect
codes in n-dimensional integer lattices via pairs (G,F) formed by
abelian groups G and homomorphisms F from Z<sup>n</sup> onto G, in the line of the Araujo-Dejter-Horak work cited above.<ref name="ADH" />

==Combinatorial designs==

Since 1994, Dejter intervened in several projects in 
[[Combinatorial design|Combinatorial Designs]] initially suggested by Alexander Rosa, C. C. Lindner
and C. A. Rodger and also worked upon with E. Mendelsohn, F. Franek,
D. Pike, P. A. Adams, E. J. Billington, D. G. Hoffman, M. Meszka and others, 
which produced results in the following subjects:

Invariants for
2-factorization and cycle systems,<ref>Dejter I. J.; Rivera-Vega  P.
I.; Rosa Alexander "Invariants for 2-factorizations and cycle systems", J.
Combin. Math. Combin. Comput., 16 (1994), 129-152.</ref>

Triangles
in 2-factorizations,<ref>Dejter I. J.; Franek F.; Mendelsohn E.;
Rosa Alexander "Triangles in 2-factorizations", Journal of Graph Theory, 26
(1997) 83-94.</ref><ref>Dejter I. J.; Franek F.; Rosa Alexander "A
Completion conjecture for Kirkman triple systems", Utilitas
Mathematica, 50 (1996) 97-102</ref>

Number of 4-cycles in
2-factorizations of complete graphs,<ref>Dejter I. J.; Lindner C.
C.; Rosa Alexander "The number of 4-cycles in 2-factorizations of K<sub>n</sub>", J.
Combin. Math. Combin. Comput., 28 (1998), 101-112.</ref>

Directed almost resolvable Hamilton-Waterloo problem,<ref>Dejter I.
J.; Pike D.; Rodger C. A. "The directed almost resolvable
Hamilton-Waterloo problem", Australas. J. Combin., 18 (1998),
201-208.</ref>

Number of 4-cycles in 2-factorizations of K<sub>2n</sub>
minus a 1-factor,<ref>Adams P. A., Billington E. J.; Lindner C. C.
"The number of 4-cycles in 2-factorizations of K<sub>2n</sub> minus a
1-factor}, Discrete Math., 220 (2000), no.1-3, 1-11.</ref>

Almost resolvable
4-cycle systems,<ref>Dejter I. J.; Lindner C. C.; Rodger C. A.;
Meszka M. "Almost resolvable 4-cycle systems", J. Combin. Math.
Combin. Comput., 63 (2007), 173-182.</ref>

Critical sets for the completion of Latin squares<ref>Horak P.; Dejter I. J. "Completing Latin squares: critical sets, II", Jour. Combin. Des., 15 (2007), 177-83.</ref>

Almost resolvable
maximum packings of complete graphs with 4-cycles.<ref>Billington E.
J.; Dejter I. J.;  Hoffman D. G.; Lindner C. C. "Almost resolvable
maximum packings of complete graphs with 4-cycles", Graphs and
Combinatorics, 27 (2011), no. 2, 161-170</ref>
